Same pattern in deleteEvent. Old code returned `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` in that branch. This is a real regression introduced by the diff.

judged_text: updateEvent's fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the predicate compares externalId against a falsy value, never matches, and selectedCalendar is always undefined where the old code returned event.destinationCalendar.externalId. Rescheduling any booking whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy bookings, plus new bookings created via the credentialId-less destination branch which this diff now stores as undefined) calls calendar.events.update with calendarId undefined — the Google call fails and the event silently stays at the old time with only a log line.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the `updateEvent` fallback was changed from `: event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `: event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. That else-branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate compares against a falsy value and will not select the intended destination calendar externalId (previously it did). This can cause `selectedCalendar` to be undefined and the update to target the wrong calendar (e.g., default/primary) or fail (e.g., 404 not found for the event id), breaking reschedule/update behavior for cases where `externalCalendarId` is missing.
